policy_title: Increase School and College Funding and Repair Buildings
stated: Increase school and college funding per pupil above the rate of inflation every year, and end the scandal of crumbling school and college buildings by investing in new buildings and clearing the backlog of repairs.

source.quote: Increase school and college funding per pupil above the rate of inflation every year, and end the scandal of crumbling school and college buildings by investing in new buildings and clearing the backlog of repairs.

bearing_set.reason: Direct per-pupil funding increases and capital investment in school/college buildings materially affect school standards, attainment, and educational opportunity.

An above-inflation per-pupil funding increase every year plus a capital programme to clear a building backlog is a large ongoing and one-off fiscal commitment; if unfunded it moves the debt path; if funded it requires revenue — a non-negligible effect on public finances sustainability.

membership_note: Clear 2-outcome bearing: the policy improves O7 (its design purpose) and generates a real fiscal cost that lands on O12 (the symmetric home for spending commitments). O13 (productivity via human capital) is a plausible long-run downstream effect but is mediated through O7 and too indirect to clear the non-negligible bar as a standalone bearing at this stage.
